title: Nth Number With Only 2, 3, 5 Factors
statement:
Consider the positive integers whose prime factors are only 2, 3 and 5. The number 1 is included, since it has no prime factors at all. In increasing order they start 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, ….

Given n, return the n-th number of this sequence, counting from 1.

examples.why: After 12 come 15, 16, 18, 20, 24. 14 = 2 · 7 and 21 = 3 · 7 are left out.

constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 1690 (so the answer fits in 32 bits)
hints: Every number in the sequence except 1 is a smaller number of the sequence times 2, 3 or 5.
Build the sequence in order. The next number is the smallest of (some earlier number × 2), (some earlier number × 3), (some earlier number × 5).

Keep three pointers, one per factor, to the earliest number whose product with that factor is not used yet. Take the minimum of the three products and advance every pointer that produced it, so 6 = 2·3 = 3·2 is added once.

explain.intuition:
Testing numbers one by one wastes time on all the numbers that are not in the sequence, and they quickly become the vast majority. Instead, generate only the good ones: each of them is an earlier good number times 2, 3 or 5.

Think of three sorted streams: the sequence times 2, times 3 and times 5. The sequence itself is these three streams merged, without duplicates. Each stream needs only a pointer into the part of the sequence already built. At each step take the smallest head, append it, and advance every stream whose head equals it.
steps: Repeat until seq has n numbers: compute a = seq[i2]·2, b = seq[i3]·3, c = seq[i5]·5.
Advance each pointer whose product equals next, using separate ifs, not else if.
pitfalls: Using else if when advancing pointers. Then 6 is produced by both the ×2 and ×3 streams and appears twice.
Forgetting that 1 is the first number, so the answer for n = 1 is 1.
Testing each integer by dividing out 2, 3 and 5. The 1690th answer is over two billion, so this never finishes.

solutions.title: Test every integer
solutions.idea: Divide out 2, 3 and 5 and see whether 1 is left. Count until the n-th hit.

solutions.title: Min-heap with a seen set
solutions.idea: Pop the smallest number n times; push its multiples by 2, 3 and 5 unless already seen.

solutions.title: Three pointers
solutions.idea: Merge the streams ×2, ×3, ×5 of the sequence built so far, advancing every pointer that ties.

followups: The allowed primes are given as a list of k primes. How do the pointers generalise, and what does it cost?
Instead of the n-th such number, find the n-th number divisible by at least one of a, b, c. Why does that one call for binary search on the answer?
